grand_strategy.reading:
Mexico is a state that cooperates with its strongest neighbour in order to keep that neighbour out of its territory, and Sheinbaum, in office since October 2024, has held that line with a steady sovereignty language. Its posture toward the United States is reluctant partnership: it hands over cartel figures, accepts CIA flights and the National Guard at the border, and refuses troops and unilateral strikes, while the USMCA stays unrenewed and the tariff exemption is the lever of the 2026 review. Mexico hedges through the EU agreement and tariffs on Chinese goods rather than through alignment with anyone, so its foreign policy is measured less by the partners it picks than by how far Washington lets it pick. Its weakest flanks are at home: a judicial reform that frightens investors, a Pemex still losing money on about USD 80bn of debt, and a remittance flow that deportations and the 1% tax are already shrinking.

Added 2026-10-16 (protagonist pass). The tariff picture has changed since the first draft: the Supreme Court ended the fentanyl tariffs on 20 February 2026 and what Washington now holds is the Section 301 duty on non-USMCA goods, the Section 232 sectoral duties and, above all, the annual review of the agreement, which is the real lever; the talks were reported stalled on 12 October with Trump asking for energy deals. The cartels work for Washington as a pretext (terrorist designations, the claim of links to the government) and for Mexico as a bargaining chip (92 transferred, El Mencho killed) at once, and the same ambivalence marks the region: Mexico shouts non-intervention over Venezuela and Peru and says little where Washington's interests bite. Its second ring is thin but real: the EU agreement, a trade deficit with China it cannot cut without hurting its own exporters, and a Latin America in which Argentina is hostile, Colombia turns cooler after the change of government in Bogota, Chile is divided from Mexico over Bachelet, and only Brazil and, since August, Peru are back in regular contact.
